newsitem.title: USA: Winter storm lashes northern California.
newsitem.headline: Winter storm lashes northern California.

text.p: A powerful winter storm lashed northern California on Tuesday, knocking out power to tens of thousands of homes and businesses, causing rivers to overflow and flooding highways.

The storm, which began early on Tuesday, dropped up to six inches (15 cm) of rain on parts of the San Francisco Bay area, turning docile rivers into raging torrents. Pacific Gas & Electric Co. (PCG.N) said 85,000 of its customers in northern and central California lost power at some point during the storm, but most had been reconnected.

Some 14,000 homes and businesses, most in the foothills of the Sierra Nevadas and along the central California coast, remained without power at midday on Tuesday, PG&E spokesman Leonard Anderson said.

The company had about 500 employees working to repair the power problems, some of them caused by high winds toppling trees, which in turn brought down power lines. The rain caused chaos on the roads and was blamed for scores of accidents.

The bad weather caused delays of up to three hours at San Francisco International Airport. The number of aircraft allowed to land there was reduced from 60 to 26 an hour on the orders of the Federal Aviation Administration, an airport spokesman said. Because of strong winds and rain, the airport was using only two runways instead of the usual four.

Many roads in the San Francisco area were flooded and about three feet (1 metre) of water and mud crashed down onto Interstate 580 in the Oakland hills near San Francisco, stranding several vehicles and forcing the closure of the highway in one direction.

The National Weather Service issued a flash flood warning in western Santa Clara and Santa Cruz counties near the central California coast, where several rivers and creeks were expected to rise above flood stage.

The San Lorenzo river burst its banks in the Felton Grove area of Felton, some 70 miles (110 kms) south of San Francisco, covering streets with up to two feet (61 cm) of water, fire officials said. The Felton Fire Department advised residents of some 18 houses in the area to be ready to move if the water rose further.
